free_tier.stated: 512 MB data storage per free cluster (0.5 GB, uncompressed BSON + indexes); one free cluster per project; 250 projects per Atlas user and 250 per organization

egress.terms: Data transfer out is not the metered axis on M0 — there is no published egress allowance or overage for Free clusters; the limits that bite are 500 connections and 100 ops/sec. Effectively unmetered for read volume, which makes M0 unusual in this class.

tooling: Standard MongoDB drivers (pymongo, motor), `mongosh`, Atlas Data API (HTTPS), `mongodump`/`mongorestore`; GridFS for files >16 MB via pymongo's gridfs
chaining: 250 projects per user x 1 free cluster each x 512 MB = ~128 GB per Atlas account, and 250 organizations per user gives another axis. GridFS chunks (255 KB default) mean no practical per-object cap beyond the 512 MB total.
limits_note: 512 MB total is tiny per unit — the whole value is the 250x multiplier. 100 ops/sec, 500 connections, no sharding, no configurable storage. Cluster creation is heavily rate-limited in practice (one free cluster per project, project creation itself throttled).
reliability_note: Free clusters are shared and throttle at 100 ops/sec; a bulk-write workload will be visibly slow rather than failing. Data is 3-node replicated, no vanishing.
confidence_note: One page read moves it to documented.
